notes: IE/PL/PT/HR current-fact reconciliation: Three current provider guidance has materially inconsistent dormancy thresholds so the cheap 80-day recommendation is withdrawn; Orange PL current official +365-day validity extension is PLN39; Yorn remains weekly-cost and blocks incoming calls/SMS after 7 days unpaid; A1 HR current first-party recharge/KYC/roaming paths are confirmed but voucher-to-validity duration remains unresolved.

routes.acquisitionSummary: Current Three Ireland provider terms and provider-moderated help agree that a prepay number can be terminated for extended inactivity, but the current guidance is internally inconsistent on the safe timing: a 2026 help article describes an alert after at least 90 days plus another 180 days before removal, while other Three guidance says to top up at least every 6 months and the General Terms permit restriction/termination after 12 months without top-up or chargeable use. Credit expiry is a separate rule. The legacy “one SMS every ~80 days” recommendation therefore overstates certainty.

keep.action: Three consistently says a top-up or credit-reducing call/text/data resets dormancy, but current provider guidance conflicts on the relevant inactivity threshold (90+180 days, six-month advice, and a 12-month contractual termination threshold). Do not publish a single cheapest cadence until Three reconciles these rules.

routes.chinaActivation: Three Prepay SIM/eSIM is an Irish consumer product. Online/self-service top-up exists, but a reliable China-first acquisition/activation path is not established in this packet.
routes.kyc: No evidence in the current Three consumer prepay flow establishes a mandatory national real-name registration regime; acquisition/activation still remains Ireland-centered for this use case.
routes.payment: My3 supports top-up and scheduled top-up; current keep-cost is not modeled because lifecycle timing is internally inconsistent.
routes.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.roamingSms: Three provider-moderated support confirms that while abroad the phone can connect automatically to a roaming network and receive calls/texts without enabling mobile-data roaming; exact OTP reliability outside the EU is not independently established.
routes.refund: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.holdReason: Current Three provider guidance conflicts on the dormancy timeline, so the prior €0.30/year / 80-day recommendation is not decision-safe. Keep as HOLD until one current lifecycle rule can be reconciled.
routes.tariffSummary: HOLD: top-up or chargeable use preserves activity, but current Three materials conflict on 90+180 days vs six-month advice vs 12-month contractual threshold.
guideSteps: HOLD: do not use the legacy 1-SMS/80-day cost model.
Wait for one current provider lifecycle rule before promotion.

routes.acquisitionSummary: Current Orange Polska prepaid pricing explicitly offers account-validity extensions of +31 days for PLN9, +93 days for PLN19, and +365 days for PLN39. The old PLN5 inactivity-maintenance fee remains abolished since 24 January 2024. Current ordinary reload validity is also amount-dependent. The legacy PLN10/year model is therefore stale.

keep.action: Current Orange prepaid page explicitly offers +365 days of account validity for PLN39. Shorter extensions are +31d/PLN9 and +93d/PLN19. The former PLN5 inactivity fee was abolished in 2024.

routes.chinaActivation: Polish prepaid numbers require registration. Orange supports several registration methods, but in-person registration accepts an identity card or passport; a reliable China-first new-number acquisition/activation path is not established.
routes.kyc: Registration is mandatory. Orange explicitly accepts identity card or passport for in-person prepaid registration.
routes.payment: Orange prepaid supports reloads and paid validity extensions; local online identity/payment rails may still make acquisition Poland-centered.
routes.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.roamingSms: Orange prepaid supports roaming; current packet does not establish China-specific incoming OTP reliability or whether all desired verification senders deliver consistently abroad.
routes.refund: The former inactivity fee was withdrawn/refunded following regulatory intervention; no refund assumption is used for current prepaid validity extensions.
routes.holdReason: Current annual validity economics are clear at PLN39/365 days, but new-number registration/acquisition remains Poland-centered and China/overseas OTP reliability is not independently verified.
routes.tariffSummary: Current official account-validity extension: PLN39 for +365 days; old PLN5 inactivity fee abolished in 2024.
guideSteps: HOLD: PLN39/365-day validity is current first-party pricing.
Require stronger foreign acquisition and overseas OTP evidence before promotion.

routes.acquisitionSummary: Current Vodafone Yorn remains a recurring tariff rather than a low-cost PAYG retention product. Vodafone states Yorn tariffs carry a weekly cost. If the tariff charge remains unpaid for 7 days after its due date, incoming calls and SMS are also blocked until sufficient balance is available and the overdue tariff cost is debited.

keep.action: Weekly-cost tariff model. If the scheduled tariff charge is not paid within 7 days, Vodafone says incoming calls and SMS are blocked; restoring sufficient balance causes the overdue tariff cost to be collected. This is structurally unsuitable for cheap passive number retention.

routes.chinaActivation: Yorn is a Portugal consumer tariff. New users can request a Yorn SIM or port a number, but the product is not designed as an overseas-first passive retention route.
routes.kyc: Yorn eligibility is generally age 35 or under, with a student exception. Signup asks for Portuguese Citizen Card number or another identification document for non-Portuguese users; one Yorn number per identity document.
routes.payment: Recurring tariff cost must remain funded; unpaid cost leads to service restrictions and later collection when balance becomes sufficient.
routes.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.roamingSms: Vodafone states Yorn works in roaming. In the EEA/UK received communications are free; outside the EEA country-specific roaming charges apply. This does not remove the underlying weekly tariff funding requirement.
routes.refund: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.holdReason: Weekly recurring tariff cost plus blocking of incoming calls/SMS after 7 days unpaid makes Yorn structurally unsuitable for cheap passive retention.
routes.tariffSummary: HOLD: weekly-cost Yorn tariff; after 7 days unpaid, incoming calls/SMS are blocked until balance covers the overdue tariff.
guideSteps: Negative-knowledge card: recurring weekly tariff is not a low-cost retention route.
Do not convert the weekly charge into a misleading annual “keep cost”.

routes.acquisitionSummary: Current A1 Croatia standard prepaid can be ordered online; current SIM promo pricing is EUR3 and physical SIM delivery requires showing an identity card, while A1 also exposes a prepaid data-registration flow accepting an identity card or passport. Current online recharge supports EUR5/10/15/20/35 standard voucher amounts and card/Apple Pay/Google Pay/Revolut/KEKS Pay/PayPal. A1 confirms those recharges extend account validity, but current first-party material captured here does not state the validity duration produced by each voucher amount.

keep.action: EUR5 is the lowest currently displayed standard voucher amount, and A1 says standard vouchers extend account validity. The captured current first-party pages do not specify how many validity days each voucher amount adds, so no yearly keep cost or safe interval is modeled.

routes.chinaActivation: A1 sells standard prepaid SIM online with delivery and first-call activation; physical delivery requires identity-card presentation. This packet does not establish international delivery or a China-first activation path.
routes.kyc: A1 offers prepaid data registration using a digital photo of an identity card or passport. Delivery of the current standard prepaid SIM requires identity-card presentation; foreign remote onboarding remains unresolved.
routes.payment: Online recharge can be made regardless of location using bank card, Apple Pay/Google Pay, Revolut, KEKS Pay or PayPal. Current standard voucher amounts start at EUR5.
routes.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
routes.roamingSms: A1 publishes a prepaid roaming tariff and says prepaid users automatically connect to available networks abroad. The packet does not establish China-specific incoming OTP reliability.
routes.holdReason: Current online acquisition/recharge/KYC/roaming evidence is stronger, but the key standard-voucher validity duration is still absent from captured current first-party material; annual retention cost cannot be calculated safely.
routes.tariffSummary: HOLD: SIM EUR3; recharge starts EUR5 and extends validity, but current first-party voucher-to-validity duration remains unresolved.
guideSteps: HOLD: do not infer a yearly keep cost from the EUR5 minimum voucher.
Re-open when current first-party voucher validity days are captured.
